skills.description: Functionality-confusion / invalid-input persistence testing. skills.name: logic-bug-hunting
skills.description: Business-logic / broken-workflow bug hunting methodology. Map the application's workflows, roles, and authentication, then violate the expected sequence: skip/reorder/replay steps, hit the final endpoint directly, decode flow 'return' params, and test whether verification (password/2FA/confirm) is enforced server-side on the final mutation or only client-side. Best where scanner-driven XSS/SQLi/CSRF are exhausted (high-report programs) but logic gaps remain. Triggers on: logic bug, broken workflow, step-skipping, verification bypass, change-email/phone flow, access control via flow.

skills.name: case-sensitivity-bypass
skills.description: Case-sensitivity / input-normalization bypass. Change the case of an email, username, domain, or key to skip a case-sensitive validation or deny-check (e.g. 'can't invite/downgrade a higher-privilege Owner/Admin'), then let the case-insensitive downstream system process it anyway — leading to role downgrade, lockout, duplicate-account, allowlist bypass, or OAuth redirect_uri/JWT host checks. Triggers on 'test@gmail.com' vs 'test@gmail.coM', case bypass, normalization inconsistency, invite/role protection bypass.

skills.name: unicode-homoglyph-bypass
skills.description: Unicode normalization / homoglyph / full-width / IDNA bypass of domain and email blocklists and host allowlists. Replace a letter with a visually-identical Unicode lookalike (e.g. 'İ' vs 'I'/'i', Cyrillic/Greek lookalikes, full-width forms) so a character-based deny/allow filter misses it, while the email/DNS/identity system normalizes (NFKC/IDNA punycode) it back to the real mailbox — bypassing owner rules like 'deny yopmail.com'. Triggers on blocked-domain invite bypass, IDN homograph, Unicode normalization attack, 0xacb normalization table.

skills.name: role-subjects-membership-bypass
skills.description: Group/role membership bypass via direct role-subjects manipulation. Triggers on PUT/PATCH /api/roles/{id} with a subjects array, add member without invite, forced group membership, membership authorization bypass, org role-subjects manipulation.

skills.name: quota-plan-limit-bypass
skills.description: Quota / plan-limit / usage-limit bypass via (A) deferred-acceptance counting (stage N invites/profiles then finalize all to exceed a paid seat/profile cap for free), (B) race conditions on a per-plan usage cap (concurrent create requests exceed the limit, e.g. 306 > 300 profiles), (C) plan-gating bypass by calling the paid/entitlement API directly with a no-plan session (client-side gating), and (D) low-privilege role reading private workspace data (members/roles/invitations/balance/plan) via un-gated API endpoints. Triggers on account takeover, reset password email swap, forge reset link, base64 reset token, CRLF/newline in email bypass, predictable reset token, reusable token, signup with existing email.

skills.name: idor-http-method-tampering
skills.description: IDOR (Insecure Direct Object Reference) combined with HTTP method/verb tampering. When an endpoint exposes a parameterized object ID (?id=197) and the access-control is tied to a specific HTTP method, change BOTH the object ID and the method (e.g. PUT -> GET) to bypass the authorization check and read/modify another user's object (PII leak). Covers enumerating sequential object IDs, verb-switching to skip a method-scoped ACL, GET-bypass-on-PUT-endpoint, and reading cross-user resources. Triggers on IDOR, change id parameter to access another user, HTTP method tampering, GET bypass on a PUT/POST endpoint, access other user's invite/profile/order/data by id.

skills.name: locked-object-idor-bypass
skills.description: Locked-object / entitlement-state IDOR bypass. When a server state-locks some of YOUR objects (free plan allows 3 lists, 4th+ is locked: no rename/edit/share) but the manage endpoints take a client-supplied object id (bookmark_id) and don't re-check the locked/entitlement state, you can act on the locked object by swapping its id into a request for an unlocked/allowed object (rename, add icon, share). Bypasses plan/feature/state locks and exposes locked resources (e.g. shareable /lists/<id> path). Distinct from cross-user IDOR: both ids are the attacker's; the flaw is a missing server-side locked-state check on mutation. Triggers on rename/edit/share a locked list by swapping its id, bypass free-plan list lock, locked-state restriction bypass, own-object IDOR, feature-gating via object id.

skills.name: js-hidden-endpoint-mass-pii
skills.description: Discover hidden/management endpoints by reviewing JS files, then get massive PII disclosure via an enumerable numeric ID parameter (mass IDOR/BOLA). Workflow: find an unadvertised endpoint in JS (e.g. /user_management.edit_user_new?p_usr_id=-1) that errors without session cookies, replay with a valid (even low-priv) session, then flip a numeric id from -1/0 to positive (p_usr_id=1, user_id=1) to dump other users' PII (100K+ rows). Also covers the sibling low-effort bug: HTML injection (HTMLi) into emails via a forgot-password/request-user form. Second pattern: Google dorking finds a search-engine-indexed path missed by wordlists, a custom 403 indicates an app-level restriction, fuzzing the discovered application root finds an unprotected report endpoint, and download exposes a large XLSX/CSV of mass PII. Triggers on hidden endpoint in JS, edit_user/user management endpoint with numeric id, p_usr_id/user_id mass enumeration, mass PII disclosure, IDOR on management API, HTMLi in email, indexed path via Google dorking, custom 403 app-level restriction, unprotected report/export endpoint, mass PII in XLSX/CSV download.

skills.name: tamperable-identity-cookie

Sequential ids make it mass PII (tens of thousands of users). Core primitive: server trusts a client-controlled encoded-but-not-signed identifier instead of a server-side session binding. Triggers on base64 cookie with user id, change user id in cookie to access another account, tamperable session identifier, /GetProfiledetails IDOR, weak identity token mass account PII.

skills.name: unauth-id-pii-and-archive-id-harvest

A low-privilege standard user swaps an object's own id for the shared parent/root id in a delete (or move/rename/purge) request -> root deleted -> whole tenant breaks and, in some apps, every account in the company is deactivated (admins + standard can no longer log in).
